newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian Finance Minister due to meet with banks.
newsitem.headline: Indian Finance Minister due to meet with banks.

text.p: Indian Finance Minister P. Chidambaram will meet with banks and financial institutions as a follow-up to the central bank's credit policy for the second half of fiscal 1996/97, newspapers said on Monday.

"The meetings, which will also focus on lending for export, agriculture and priority sectors, will be kicked off with the State Bank of India," The Business Standard newspaper said, quoting finance ministry sources.
The meetings will be held in Bombay on November 8 and 9.

The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) on Saturday in its monetary policy for the second half of 1996/97 ending March, announced steps to boost liquidity, raise export credit and increase the flow of bank funds into stock and commodity markets.
It announced a cut of two percentage points in banks' cash reserve requirement (CRR) staggered over the next four months, releasing more than 85 billion rupees ($2.4 billion) into the banking system.
